thread:
Amina: Incoming invoice from MarketLayer for platform fees shows 13% VAT (CAD) but vendor claims they are a marketplace seller and that OSS/marketplace rules apply. Invoice ML-2026-2001, amount CAD 26,000, VAT CAD 3,380. Link: https://invoices.example.com/ML-2026-2001.pdf

Diego: Marketplace vs supplier responsibility matters. If MarketLayer is the operator who collects/remits VAT under marketplace rules, we shouldn't be charged VAT on the vendor's fee. Do we have their marketplace operator OSS registration?

Amina: Vendor attached a PDF saying "collected by MarketLayer Ltd" with operator VAT GB987654321. But the invoice footer still shows VAT charged by the seller entity (MapleServices Inc). Confusing.

Nora: AP: Hold payment until clarified. If operator remits, vendor should reissue net invoice or provide operator invoice showing VAT remittance. Otherwise treat as VAT charged and reclaim via input VAT where applicable.

TaxOps: Quick checklist: 1) Confirm operator is registered and included as collector on invoice. 2) Check if transaction falls within Canadian digital services rules (nexus). 3) If operator collects, we need operator invoice or evidence of VAT remittance. Otherwise we record input VAT and include in Canadian GST/HST filing.

Amina: Reached out to MarketLayer: "Please confirm whether you (MarketLayer Ltd) collected VAT on behalf of MapleServices and provide operator invoice or proof of remittance." Vendor replied: "We are the seller, not the operator. We mistakenly included operator note. We'll remove VAT and reissue." :white_check_mark:

AP-bot: Event: invoice_hold placed (invoice=ML-2026-2001, reason=vat_marketplace_claim)

Diego: If they reissue net, ensure Coupa stores both original and corrected invoice for audit. If they insist on VAT charged, request operator remittance evidence and tag TaxOps for refund filing.

Amina: Will monitor and update thread. Thanks.
